newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Manila deals keep Vietnam rice market on boil.
newsitem.headline: Manila deals keep Vietnam rice market on boil.

text.p: The Philippines' regional rice- buying spree kept traders in Vietnam on their toes in an otherwise quiet post-holiday market, dealers said on Wednesday.
Most foreign buyers were sidelined, waiting for harvesting of the Mekong Delta's new crop to get under way in mid-March, which left prices barely changed from a week ago.
Traders said five-percent broken grade rice, FOB Saigon Port, was unchanged at $265-270 per tonne, 10 percent broken was about $5 lower at $255-260 and 25 percent broken was steady at $230-238.
Manila's Department of Agriculture said on Wednesday that the state-owned National Food Authority had signed a contract to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from China.

Traders said the deal was similar to an agreement, signed this month, under which Manila would buy 100,000 tonnes of 25 percent broken rice from Vietnam's state-owned food corporation at $291.50 a tonne and take an option on a further 100,000 tonnes.
One trader said 56,000 tonnes of the first 100,000 tonnes of Vietnamese rice would be shipped in March and the remainder would be shipped in April.
Traders said the Philippines' latest deal with China, probably specified optional origin for the grain, with Pakistan or Vietnam being likely optional sources.
"I doubt if it would be Chinese rice," said one. "Maybe there's an option on Pakistan or Vietnamese rice, otherwise it wouldn't make sense."

Both agreements follow President Fidel Ramos' approval for the Philippines to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice to beef up the country's buffer stocks before July. Rice supply in the Philippines is normally low in the third quarter of the year.
Activity was low in Saigon Port, where three vessels were loading with roughly 30,000 tonnes of rice bound for Indonesia.

The Mekong Delta's coming harvest will be at least a month late because of heavy flooding in the area last year. Traders said the delay could make the summer crop late, raising the possibility of harvesting during rains in July and August.

Despite that problem, Vietnam is hoping for record exports of up to 3.5 million tonnes of rice this year. The country sold more than three million tonnes abroad last year, making it the world's third-largest exporter after Thailand and the United States.
